strings.name: Li Qiang
strings.role: Premier of the People’s Republic of China; member of the CPC Politburo Standing Committee
strings.summary: Li Qiang rose from local government in Zhejiang to national leadership, heading the Party organizations in Jiangsu and Shanghai before becoming premier in 2023. His career spans private enterprise, foreign investment and regional cooperation, alongside controversy over Shanghai’s Covid lockdown.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through 18 November 2026, with recent activity documented at the 16 November Manila meeting. Party posts, state appointments, acting and elected governorships, and economic targets and results are distinguished.
strings.influence.rationale: Advanced from local government into the leadership of China’s State Council, participating in economic management, industrial policy and foreign economic and trade affairs.
strings.facts.f1.label: Early life
strings.facts.f1.value: Born in July 1959, he is from Rui’an, Zhejiang. He began work in July 1976 and joined the Communist Party of China in April 1983; official biographies give no day of birth.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: He studied agricultural mechanization, took management engineering courses, and earned a Central Party School postgraduate qualification and a Hong Kong Polytechnic University EMBA. Coursework, educational qualifications and degrees are recorded separately.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Industry and business policy
strings.highlights.h1.text: He promoted foreign investment while leading Shanghai. Reuters linked him to Tesla’s factory project; production began in 2019, and local authorities also supported its 2022 reopening. The projects involved the company and multiple government bodies.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Shanghai lockdown and public services
strings.highlights.h2.text: While he was Shanghai Party secretary in 2022, the city underwent roughly two months of lockdown. Human Rights Watch reported obstacles to food and non-Covid medical care. These criticisms are important to assessments of his governance.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Attends China–ASEAN meeting in Manila
strings.timeline.t1.text: As premier, he attended the 29th China–ASEAN leaders’ meeting, advocating free trade and regional cooperation. Proposals for further cooperation in his speech were policy positions.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Sets annual economic targets
strings.timeline.t2.text: The government work report set a 2026 growth target of 4.5–5% and emphasized employment. This was an annual target, not an achieved full-year growth rate.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Appointed premier
strings.timeline.t3.text: Following a decision of the first session of the 14th National People’s Congress, President Xi Jinping signed an order appointing Li Qiang premier, succeeding Li Keqiang. They are distinct individuals.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Joins the Politburo Standing Committee
strings.timeline.t4.text: The first plenum of the 20th CPC Central Committee elected him to the Politburo Standing Committee. This Party election was separate from his appointment as premier the following year.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Shanghai announces new Party secretary
strings.timeline.t5.text: A Shanghai officials’ meeting announced the central leadership’s decision appointing Li Qiang Party secretary, succeeding Han Zheng. He also joined the Politburo that year; Party secretary and mayor are separate posts.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Jiangsu announces new Party secretary
strings.timeline.t6.text: A Jiangsu officials’ meeting announced that Li Qiang would succeed Luo Zhijun as provincial Party secretary. The date here is that of the meeting announcing the central decision.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Elected governor of Zhejiang
strings.timeline.t7.text: The first session of Zhejiang’s 12th People’s Congress elected him governor. He had been appointed vice-governor and acting governor on 21 December 2012; the two stages are recorded separately.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Becomes Wenzhou Party secretary
strings.timeline.t8.text: He had previously worked in Zhejiang’s civil affairs and industry and commerce administration. In 2004 he became secretary-general of the Zhejiang Party committee, subsequently advancing within the provincial leadership.
